title: Phase Two — Architecture, File Map, and Twenty Improvements

headings.text: Phase Two — Architecture, File Map, and Twenty Improvements
Twenty-plus concrete improvements over phase one

excerpt: B"H Boruch Hashem Blessed is He Phase Two — Architecture, File Map, and Twenty Improvements The Awtsmoos draws a line from canonical source to living post without division or disguise; Awtsmoos.com should make each module small enough that future eyes can see why it exists and where it lies. Observed code facts modules
searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase two — architecture, file map, and twenty improvements the awtsmoos draws a line from canonical source to living post without division or disguise; awtsmoos.com should make each module small enough that future eyes can see why it exists and where it lies. observed code facts modules/chitas/ already creates a virtual daily chitas series. living path/cards.js contains an explicit chabad.org external redirect and suppresses social actions for virtualstudy. api/comments.js already supports versesection, which can anchor verse level discussion without inventing a second comment api. normal post cards navigate to /heichelos/{heichel}/series/{series}/{post}. a new torah library layer exists with torahlibrary.js, torahlibraryids.js, and torahlibrarypresentation.js, but it currently models root/domain/work/page virtual bookshelf ids, not a generic verse range post abstraction. no existing dynamicpost, referencepost, contentrefs, or range reference abstraction was found. proposed module graph dynamic reference/reference contract.js → validates ordered source references and stable identity. dynamic reference/reference id.js → creates/parses url safe dynamic post ids. dynamic reference/reference registry.js → dispatches a reference to a source adapter. dynamic reference/post composer.js → resolves ordered ranges and returns a normal post like reader model. chitas/range reference.js → converts aliyah boundary metadata into canonical tanach range references. chitas/week state.js → url/query date, language, israel/diaspora, previous/next/today helpers. chitas/dynamic post.js → reconstructs one chitas dynamic post from stable post id + query state. chitas/week controls.js → pure control model for ui renderers. existing chitas/schedule.js and virtual series.js → produce native internal cards and selected week data, never external urls. existing living path/cards.js → delete the chabad specific branch; chitas follows normal post navigation/social. normal post reader entry → intercept daily chitas dynamic ids and obtain post body through post composer; all ordinary posts untouched. exact likely touched files new modules under geelooy/heichelos/heichel/modules/dynamic reference/ and modules/chitas/. existing chitas schedule/series/card renderer. one reader/router integration file once located by direct route inspection. focused css modules for chitas week controls/reader masthead if the reader has modular style manifests. tests under tests/geelooy/. twenty plus concrete improvements over phase one 1. keep source reference shape independent from chitas. 2. keep calendar date outside canonical torah range identity where possible. 3. use stable dynamic post id as the comment thread post identity. 4. preserve versesection for comments bound to canonical verses. 5. never encode human language labels as source keys. 6. separate resolver errors from scheduler errors. 7. make language a presentation/resolution option, not a different torah identity. 8. keep israel/diaspora in week state because it changes schedule selection. 9. normalize all date math at local noon to avoid utc day drift. 10. make previous/next week exactly ±7 local days. 11. make today remove stale date override instead of accumulating query cruft. 12. maintain direct reload urls after every selector change. 13. make the week list chronologically sunday→shabbos. 14. highlight selected day separately from today. 15. keep card social actions available because the card is now a normal post. 16. ensure card click never reads externalhref. 17. use the normal comments api; no chitas specific backend comments endpoint. 18. compose content from canonical source records rather than copy/paste torah text into the chitas object. 19. provide source provenance in the reader ui without exposing external study destinations. 20. cache at resolver boundary, not schedule boundary. 21. add abortcontroller to asynchronous source resolution. 22. keep every new js/css module under 120 lines. 23. add explicit b"h / boruch hashem / blessed is he poetic module headers. 24. use tabs in every touched source file. 25. no partial modifications: every existing touched file is rewritten completely. 26. test normal non chitas post cards after removing the special external branch. 27. test comments visibility on dynamic chitas posts. 28. test hard reload of a deep chitas post url. 29. test share/copy url reconstructs same week/language. 30. test graceful internal error if torah source resolution fails. dependency graph schedule metadata → chitas range adapter → generic reference contract → source resolver → post composer → existing reader → existing comments/social. week query state → chitas series loader + reader masthead. living path cards → normal internal post route → same dynamic reconstruction path on click or reload. the critical invariant is one way: no dynamic post may become the canonical torah source. the canonical source feeds the composed vessel; the vessel never owns the torah it reveals.

title: Phase Three — Final Critique and Thirty Additional Improvements

headings.text: Phase Three — Final Critique and Thirty Additional Improvements

excerpt: B"H Boruch Hashem Blessed is He Phase Three — Final Critique and Thirty Additional Improvements The Awtsmoos asks the plan to stand trial before a single source file is stirred; Awtsmoos.com must prove the architecture can survive reload, mobile fingers, comments, and every remembered word. What phase two still risked
searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase three — final critique and thirty additional improvements the awtsmoos asks the plan to stand trial before a single source file is stirred; awtsmoos.com must prove the architecture can survive reload, mobile fingers, comments, and every remembered word. what phase two still risked the previous plan could still over assume the shape of the tanach corpus. the repository has a torah library bookshelf but the actual rich post reader may use a separate canonical post model. therefore the generic reference contract must be adapter driven and must not hard code wikisource page ids. chitas can initially use whichever internal tanach adapter the real reader already uses, while the abstraction remains capable of supporting ordinary post ranges. thirty plus additional corrections 1. do not implement source resolution until the exact reader entry module and internal tanach payload are read. 2. if tanach text is already ordinary heichel posts, prefer post range references first. 3. if tanach has a specialized api, keep it behind tanach range adapter. 4. the generic contract should allow multiple source kinds without optional field soup. 5. validate ranges on creation and again on resolution. 6. canonical ids must be deterministic across language changes. 7. dynamic post ids must never contain raw translated book names. 8. a chitas card description may show the reference but must not be the reader body source. 9. week selection must update both list and opened dynamic post coherently. 10. reader language toggle must not accidentally shift to another calendar week. 11. date picker must accept any civil date, then derive its sunday week anchor. 12. hebrew labels should include hebrew weekday/parsha names where metadata exists. 13. english mode should preserve hebrew title as secondary context, not erase it. 14. directionality must be scoped to torah text, not flip the global navigation chrome. 15. reader typography should inherit native tanach tokens before adding chitas accents. 16. do not create an iframe or duplicate scroll container. 17. bottom mobile dock must not cover the final verse or comment composer. 18. reader masthead controls must wrap cleanly at 320px. 19. all buttons/selectors must have accessible labels and at least 44px, preferably 48px, hit size. 20. week navigation should work with keyboard as well as touch. 21. preserve browser back/forward semantics when changing week/date. 22. if controls use history.pushstate, popstate must reconstruct state. 23. avoid fetching seven full torah ranges just to display seven list cards; resolve full text only after opening one post. 24. list cards should remain lightweight schedule metadata. 25. reader post resolution should fetch only the selected range. 26. comments count on list cards may stay lazy; comments ui must load on reader. 27. stable dynamic post thread identity should include date when the same canonical range can recur in different chitas contexts, unless product semantics explicitly want one shared thread. 28. verse level comments should always map back to canonical source identity so torah discussion can be reused. 29. unit tests should distinguish thread identity from source identity. 30. simchas torah special references need explicit adapter rules because phrases like “through the end” are not ordinary fixed strings. 31. isru chag “from beginning through portion” requires a cumulative bereishis range, not just a display sentence. 32. festival deferral behavior must be tested with actual internal range construction. 33. if source resolution cannot map a book alias, error internally with useful context rather than redirect externally. 34. no code path should mention chabad.org after migration, except historical docs/tests if explicitly retained. 35. search the changed subtree for externalhref, virtualstudy, and chabad host before completion. 36. search for generic card vertical decorative labels that can collide on mobile; chitas custom layout should avoid them. 37. preserve ordinary living path grouping behavior and owner controls. 38. dynamic posts are read only compositions unless a future explicit persistence flow is built. 39. do not let edit/delete governance controls appear on virtual dynamic chitas posts. 40. do let social/comment/share controls appear where ordinary read only posts permit them. 41. add a resolver provenance field for debugging, but do not expose internal implementation noise to ordinary users. 42. add concise internal loading skeleton rather than the large fallback panel shown in the screenshot. 43. verify no cls/scroll jump when text resolves. 44. verify selected language and date persist after hard reload. 45. verify selecting another week while a post is open gives a predictable reader/list transition. final architecture after critique the generic dynamic reference layer defines identity and composition but knows nothing about calendars. a source registry chooses internal adapters. chitas is a producer: schedule metadata becomes canonical range references only when a particular day is opened. living path list cards remain light native posts. the existing reader remains the presentation/social owner. chitas contributes a masthead and week state controls, not a parallel reader. this is the least magical architecture: every behavior can be reconstructed from url + canonical source + schedule metadata, and every comment or progress marker has an explicit stable identity.
